prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: one complete transparent PNG snake miniature on a neutral round tabletop base, for 48/64/96px RPG display.
Primary request: replace the brown snake in Image 1 with the LARGE WHITE SNAKE identity in Image 2, completely changing its pose to an open S. Image 1 is the edit target only for the dark grey-brown thin circular disc, subdued bronze-grey bevel, steep downward three-quarter view, soft upper-left light and matte painted sculpted finish. Do NOT keep its closed circular coil. Image 2 is the native white-snake identity reference.
Subject and anatomy: exactly one complete large ivory-white snake, a natural thick-bodied snake with one low, flat, slightly wedge-shaped snake head, small dark natural eyes, a restrained small forked tongue, and a tapering single tail. No hood, horns, wings, fins, legs, crest, spines or rattle. The head is a readable modest part of the complete body, not a giant portrait.
Pose and silhouette: a loose OPEN S with two broad opposing bends and clearly visible dark base between them; no closed donut, spiral knot or piled coil. Lay most of the body low on the disc. Put the head slightly lifted at lower-left, looking left and a little toward the viewer. The thick body curves from the head through centre-left toward upper-middle, then bends down toward the right half and ends in an inward-pointing tail near lower-right. Keep an unmistakable continuous snake body from head to tail, with no overlapping body junction that could suggest two snakes. The whole figure remains well inside the disc and leaves open areas of dark disc around the S. It must contrast strongly with Image 1's closed brown ring and with a cobra's upright broad hood.
Colour/material: warm ivory-white scales across large readable planes; restrained cool grey shadows underneath and at bends, slightly creamy belly scutes where visible. The white is matte animal colour, not glow, snow or magic. Broad sculpted scale groupings give volume; do not make tiny scales the sole identifying feature. No fish fin edge or eel head.
Framing and shared base: square 1024x1024 canvas; centred nearly circular neutral dark grey-brown thin disc around 86% of canvas width, a thin subdued bronze-grey bevel as in Image 1. Snake spans about 80–86% of the disc diameter. Keep every tip including tongue and tail inside the base with an exposed perimeter strip. Top-right 23% by 18% of canvas must contain no head or critical feature for runtime badges; do not draw a badge or guide.
Soft upper-left illumination and only small contact shading on the disc. Slightly exaggerated clean body planes for small-size recognition, no bright outline or bloom.
Backdrop: genuine transparent native alpha outside the round disc, clean antialiased edges, no outside cast shadow.
Avoid: closed ring coil, cobra hood, horns, wings, fins, extra heads, extra snakes, scenery, grass, stones, ice, fog, faction rings, coloured rim, rank, crowns, HP, shields, selection, text, numbers, icons, watermark, black/white backdrop, painted checkerboard. Exactly one snake and one neutral base; a single asset rather than a sheet.
reference_roles: Style/base edit target and negative pose contrast; retain disc/material/light/camera, replace closed brown ring with open ivory S.
Native large white snake identity reference; plain natural snake without hood, horns or wings.
image_processing: Original built-in image_gen output copied byte-for-byte. No image pixel edit, recolouring, matte, or alpha replacement.

observations: Ivory-white open S posture and neutral base match the family direction.

ANATOMY FAILURE: upper-right body end remains blunt and thick, while a separate tapering tail-like segment emerges at lower right. The visible path does not establish one unambiguous head-to-tail body.
review.selection_reason: Reject this version; parent approved one targeted built-in imagegen repair to create a single continuous tapering tail at the upper body end and remove the lower-right extra segment.
remaining_limits: Original failed candidate retained; do not use as final runtime master.
